why: Monotonic squared sums identify which boundary can move, so one unsuccessful test removes an entire boundary choice.
quantitative_comparison: The complete baseline has (U+1)(U+2)/2 candidate pairs. The two-pointer loop has at most U+1 iterations because each move narrows the gap by one. This compares worst-case candidate bounds, not an observed time ratio; either method can stop earlier on a match.
tradeoffs: Requires nonnegative input, a suitable sqrt bound and widened squared-sum arithmetic. A one-loop search using a square-root test is another O(sqrt(c)) alternative, so the archive is not asymptotically better than every reasonable method.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
